title: Korean Clothes Sizing: How to Read the Label and Buy Online

hero.intro: Korean clothes sizing catches almost everyone out the first time. A medium from Seoul is not a US medium, and some tags carry no letter at all. Here is how to read the label, which numbers to trust, and how to order online with fewer surprises.

sections.heading: Why korean clothes sizing runs small
paragraphs: Korean makers draw their patterns around a different average frame. Many of them also cut close to the body and leave less spare room. So a letter from a Korean label often sits a size or so under the same letter from a US brand. Sleeves and hems tend to come up shorter. Shoulder seams sit closer together, for a narrower frame.

None of this is a flaw. It is a different starting point, and it means korean clothes sizes need reading, not guessing. Most korean fashion wear sits close to the body by design, so there is little spare fabric to borrow. The korean fashion clothes women order online tend to go wrong in the same three places: shoulders, sleeves and length. Check those three first and most of the guesswork goes.

sections.heading: Free size, one letter, and the 55/66 numbers
paragraphs: Many pieces from Korea arrive with a single letter on the tag, or with Free size and nothing else. Free size means one cut with no grading, drawn to cover a range of bodies. It works on a floaty dress, wide trousers or an oversized knit. It is a risky bet on anything with a waist seam, a zip or a fitted sleeve.

You may also see numbers. A korean clothes size printed as 55 or 66 comes from an older system that runs alongside the letters. The numbers and the letters do not line up exactly, and they shift from maker to maker. Our size guide has a rough translation table, and it says plainly that the table is a guide, not a rule.

Search size chart korean clothes and you will find dozens of tables. They rarely agree, because korean clothes sizing shifts from one maker to the next. Thai makers use letters and Free size the same way, so treat every chart as a place to start. Your own numbers decide the rest.

sections.heading: Flat measurements beat the letter
paragraphs: A letter tells you which shelf a piece came from. A measurement tells you whether it will fit. So the most useful habit in korean clothes sizing is simple: compare numbers, not letters. Where a piece lists its own measurements on the product page, those come first, ahead of any chart.

To use them, measure something you already own and love. Lay it flat on a table, smooth it out, and take the numbers below. Then hold them against the piece you want. A little extra room at the waist is easy to live with, because a waist is easy to take in. A gap across the bust or the shoulders is not.
bullets: Bust: armpit to armpit, straight across, then double it.
Waist: straight across the narrowest point, then double it.
Shoulder: seam to seam across the back.
Sleeve: from the shoulder seam down to the cuff.
Length: from the top of the shoulder to the hem.

sections.heading: Petite meaning in clothes, and why Asian cuts often suit it
paragraphs: Here is the short petite clothes definition. Petite is a length grading, not a smaller size. A petite pattern keeps the bust, waist and hip of the regular size, then takes length out of the torso, the arm and the leg. So a petite clothing size starts from your usual numbers around the body. Only the lengths move.

This is the quiet upside of asian petite fashion. Many Korean and Thai pieces already run shorter in the sleeve, the body and the hem. On a shorter frame they often land close to right, with no trip to the tailor. On a long torso the same piece can come up short, so check the length line before anything else. For the longer answer to what does petite clothes mean, read our petite explainer.

paragraphs: Size runs from Korea and Thailand are short at the top end. Some stop at a large, and others go further. Some shapes reach further than their label suggests. Wrap dresses, tie and elastic waists, oversized knits and A-line cuts all have room to give. Fitted blazers, straight skirts and anything with a set waistband hold you to the number.

If you need plus size petite fashion, that is two needs at once: more room around and less length. Petite clothing plus size is still rare in Asian size runs. So tell us what you are hunting for through our contact page. Shopper notes shape what we ask makers for on the next buying round.

Buying korean wear online means trading the fitting room for five minutes with a tape measure. Once you have a routine, it is a fair trade.

These checks take the gamble out of korean clothes sizing on our site and on any other korean fashion websites you use. They hold for a kpop fashion online store and for thai clothes online shopping too, because the makers behind them use the same labels.
bullets: Know your numbers: bust, waist, hips, shoulder and inseam, saved in your phone.
Open the Size guide button on the product page and find your row.
Read any measurements listed with the piece, then compare them with a garment you own.
Read the fabric line: a stretch knit forgives a size, woven cotton and linen do not.

faqs.q: What does women's petite clothes mean?
faqs.a: It means the pattern runs shorter, not narrower. A petite piece keeps the bust, waist and hip of the regular size and takes length out of the torso, sleeve and leg. You still pick your usual size around the body. The word petite only tells you the seams sit closer together, so a hem lands where the designer meant it to.

faqs.q: Do Korean clothes run smaller than US sizes?
faqs.a: Often, yes. In korean clothes sizing, a letter usually sits about one US size under the same letter here, and sleeves and hems come up shorter. That is a pattern, not a rule, because every maker grades its own way. Use the size guide as a starting point, then check any measurements listed with the piece before you choose.

faqs.q: What does Free size actually fit?
faqs.a: Free size is one cut with no grading, meant to cover a range rather than a single size. It is a good bet on a floaty dress, wide-leg trousers or an oversized knit. It is the wrong bet on anything with a waist seam, a zip or a set-in sleeve. Compare your largest measurement with any flat measurement listed, and leave a little room.

faqs.q: I am between two sizes. Which one should I pick?
faqs.a: Let the fabric choose. Size up for woven cotton, linen, denim and anything with a zip or a fixed waist, because there is no give to borrow. Stay true for ribbed knits and jersey with stretch, which come back to shape. If your bust and your waist point at different sizes, buy for the bust and take the waist in.
